rows.why: In front view A's wide chest overhangs forelegs that tuck in under it with a ledge; B forelegs drop straight from the chest sides and the upper legs blend into the body in side view.
In side view A legs are stubby with round knobs at the elbow and knee; B legs are straighter columns and its shoulders and upper arms carry fuller muscle in front view.
The beetle is near-identical; B legs are a touch thicker at the femur with a small joint step, A legs taper smoothly, and neither reads better.
B neck narrows just under the head and widens toward the coils (front view), so the head reads as its own mass; A neck is a uniform-width tube.
B forearms are bulkier and the thighs separate with a visible gap between the legs (front and 3/4 views); A legs nearly merge into one block under the belly.
A knees bulge as round knobs between thigh and shin (front and 3/4 views); B legs taper more evenly through the knee with fuller thighs.
Tiny lizard is effectively identical; head, eyes and mouth match and B upper arms are only a hair thicker.
Close call: A limb roots bulge out at the shoulders (top and front views) and the hind knee is knobby in side view; B legs are fuller and blend more smoothly into the barrel body.
Very close: A thighs carry a bit more mass at the hip but step at the hind knee, B legs are slimmer and smoother; neither is clearly better.
Scorpion is near-identical in every view; B pincer-arm root is slightly rounder in the head close-up, too small to matter.
Slight: B head is a little larger and rounder with a wider mouth, and the body flares wider below the neck (front view), so head and body read as distinct masses; A is closer to a uniform tube.
B thigh has a fuller drumstick shape at the hip tapering to the knee (side view), more believable for a biped; A thighs are thinner, straighter tubes.
A hind leg has a lumpy round bulge at the knee (side view) and its forelegs are knobby in front view; B legs are smooth thick columns with the thigh blending into the haunch.
In front view A chest balloons out over forelegs that pinch in beneath it, and its hind leg is lumpy at the knee in side view; B forelegs drop straight from the chest and the thighs taper cleanly.
B upper arms carry a rounded shoulder and elbow mass and the belly sits a little deeper (front view); A arms are thinner, flatter tubes.
The ant renders are effectively identical in every view (segments, mandibles, eyes, legs).
A thighs bulge then step at the knee into a thinner shin (front and 3/4 views); B legs taper smoothly from hip to ankle.
Slight: in front view B neck tapers more gradually into a narrower throat so the head reads as its own mass; A's body widens right below the head.
A legs are knobby, with a bulging hind knee over a thin shin (side view) and shoulders that flare out past the body (front view); B legs are fuller pillars set under the body.
B thighs and upper forelegs are fuller and blend into a slightly deeper torso (side view, 1.3 m vs 1.2 m tall); A legs read as thin sticks under the body.
